text:
alex: Hey team, started a canary on 16xA100 w/ tp=8 and saw memory spikes around kv-cache priming for seq_len=2k. peak per-GPU mem jumped ~1.8GB during NCCL all-to-all, we didn't see that on 8-GPU runs.
maria: Ugh. Is this during the kernel fallback path or regular fast kernels?
alex: Profiling shows fallback to a memcpy-heavy kernel on some attention configs. NCCL allocs + per-rank tempbufs seem to multiply. stacktrace snippet: `ncclAllToAll -> allocate_comm_scratch -> cudaMalloc` (hot)
derek: Do we still allocate per-stream comm buffers for each shard? thought we pooled them.
joyce: We do pool but only for the comm pool lifetime; for small-ish ops we still carve ephemeral workspaces. Looks like kv-cache prefetch is requesting full shard buffers leading to many ephemeral allocations.
maria: Can you paste the perf numbers? batch size, tokens/sec, alloc churn?
alex: Canary run: batch=4, max_total_tokens=8192, dynamic batching off. Profiling heatmap attached (can't attach here) but easy numbers: 16 GPUs => comm scratch peak 2.1GB, 8 GPUs => 600MB. Allocation count spike ~4x during step 1-3 of generation.
derek: Hypothesis: kernel selection chooses a variant that needs pinned staging buffer per TP shard, and kv prefetch loops allocate temp tensors per shard sequentially instead of reusing. We should: 1) clip kv prefetch to active batch seq_len; 2) reuse a device-local workspace across shards; 3) change NCCL buffer allocation to lazy pooled buffers.
joyce: Agreed. Also consider shrinking default per-shard temp reservation to a proportional heuristic: temp_reserve = min(estimated_shard_size * 0.15, 256MB). That would cap OOMs for long seq.
maria: Any quick mitigation to unblock customers?
alex: Short term: enable kv prefetch clipping flag and force kernel hint to use inplace attention kernel (no pinned staging). Patch: `--kv-prefetch-limit=active_seq` and `KERSEL_HINT=fast_inplace`.
derek: I'll prototype comm-buffer compaction: allocate a single NCCL scratch slab per-device on startup and sub-allocate with alignment. Fallback to cudaMalloc only if slab is exhausted. Should remove the per-op cudaMalloc churn.
joyce: Sounds good. Need to coordinate with allocator tuning so suballocations don't conflict with workspace pooling. Maybe expose an admission policy: comm_slab_reserve_pct.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: canary branch nccl-comm-slab-v1 queued. Tests: intra-node 16x/32x, perf regression check, mem-leak scan.
maria: OK let's run that canary. alex + derek, pair on reproducer and add a minimal script that triggers kv prefetch + tp=8. If we can get deterministic repro we'll run CI load.
alex: On it. I'll add logs for `cudaMalloc` stack and nvprof markers. Expect an update in ~2 hours. :rocket:
derek: I'll push the slab allocator sketch to my branch and add a toggled flag. If tests pass we'll wire it behind an opt-in config.
joyce: And I'll write the heuristic to clip prefetch per-batch and an integration test that verifies comm slab reuse (no new allocations after warmup).
maria: Thanks. If this fixes the spike we should also add a regression test to catch it next time (16+ GPUs, kv-prefetch=full).
alex: Yep. Will also add a short doc blurb explaining tradeoffs of kv-prefetch vs comm-memory and recommended defaults.
joyce: FYI: other customers saw similar OOMs with long contexts + tp, so high impact.
maria: Great. Keep updates in this thread.
alex: Update: pushed reproducer + nvprof logs to the canary bucket. Link in #eng-runtime later.
